tile_format.header: 32 bytes little-endian: magic 'INCO', u16 version, u16 var_code, u16 width, u16 height, u16 depth_count, u16 data_type(1=float32), f32 min, f32 max, 8 reserved
tile_format.payload: float32 little-endian, row-major, row 0 = southernmost latitude; NaN = no data

ibr.title: INCOIS Bio-ROMS (IBR) Indian Ocean surface fields
ibr.institution: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS)
ibr.producers: P. K. Ghoshal, A. P. Joshi & K. Chakraborty
ibr.time_resolution: monthly (timestamps exactly as stored in source TIME variable)
ibr.vertical_levels: surface only (no subsurface levels in source)
ibr.regridding: bilinear from native grid to 0.125 deg cell centres; any NaN corner yields NaN (no extrapolation)

armor3d.title: ARMOR3D REP - TSHUVMld Global Ocean Observation-based Product
armor3d.vertical_levels: surface (depth 0 m) only in local subset
armor3d.note: Observation-based analysis (assimilates in-situ profiles incl. Argo); not a numerical model. Velocities are geostrophic (thermal wind), not total currents.

argo.title: Argo profiling floats (GDAC NetCDF)
argo.institution: Argo GDAC (Coriolis / FR GDAC); per-float data centre recorded in profile metadata
argo.reference: Argo (2000). Argo float data and metadata from Global Data Assembly Centre (Argo GDAC). SEANOE. https://doi.org/10.17882/42182

mhw_intensity.long_name: Monthly-mean marine heatwave intensity ratio (SST - clim) / (p90 - clim), fixed 1990-2019 baseline
mhw_intensity.on_demand: any IBR timestep (derived from its SST tile)

climatology.percentile_method: numpy nanpercentile (linear interpolation) over the 30 baseline years
climatology.window: calendar month (no day-of-year smoothing; monthly data)

detrended.method: per-cell least-squares linear trend of the deseasonalised 1980-2019 monthly SST removed relative to the baseline midpoint 2005.0; mean and p90 then recomputed over the baseline

mhw_intensity.caveat: Monthly-mean marine-heatwave index: Hobday et al. (2018) categories applied to monthly-mean IBR SST against a fixed 1990-2019 monthly climatology. The >= 5-day duration criterion cannot be checked on monthly data, so this indicates months whose mean exceeded the 90th percentile, not verified heatwave events. A fixed baseline still counts part of the long-term warming as heatwave; see the detrended variant and the daily OISST index.

mhw_detrended.long_name: Monthly-mean marine heatwave intensity ratio on linearly detrended SST
mhw_detrended.on_demand: any IBR timestep (derived from its SST tile)

climatology.percentile_method: numpy nanpercentile (linear interpolation) over the 30 baseline years
climatology.window: calendar month (no day-of-year smoothing; monthly data)

detrended.method: per-cell least-squares linear trend of the deseasonalised 1980-2019 monthly SST removed relative to the baseline midpoint 2005.0; mean and p90 then recomputed over the baseline

mhw_detrended.caveat: Detrended monthly-mean MHW index: the per-cell linear 1980-2019 SST trend is removed before comparing with the 1990-2019 climatology (Jacox et al. 2020 shifting baseline), so this isolates short-term extremes from long-term warming. Monthly data: no >= 5-day rule.

chl_bloom.long_name: Chlorophyll bloom anomaly index (log10 CHL - clim) / (p90 - clim)
chl_bloom.on_demand: any IBR timestep (derived from its chlorophyll tile)

climatology.percentile_method: numpy nanpercentile (linear interpolation) over the 30 baseline years

chl_bloom.caveat: Chlorophyll bloom anomaly index from IBR model chlorophyll (monthly): the MHW ratio method applied to log10(CHL) against a 1990-2019 per-cell monthly climatology and 90th percentile. High chlorophyll marks unusually strong phytoplankton biomass; it does NOT identify harmful species or toxins, so it is a screening indicator for harmful algal blooms, not a HAB detection.

current_u.caveat: Currents are CMEMS ARMOR3D surface GEOSTROPHIC velocities only (thermal-wind balance): no wind-driven (Ekman) component, no Stokes (wave) drift, no tides or inertial motion.

current_v.caveat: Currents are CMEMS ARMOR3D surface GEOSTROPHIC velocities only (thermal-wind balance): no wind-driven (Ekman) component, no Stokes (wave) drift, no tides or inertial motion.

vorticity.long_name: Relative vorticity of the surface geostrophic flow
vorticity.method: (1/(R cos phi)) (dv/dlambda - d(u cos phi)/dphi), central differences, R = 6371 km
vorticity.caveat: Currents are CMEMS ARMOR3D surface GEOSTROPHIC velocities only (thermal-wind balance): no wind-driven (Ekman) component, no Stokes (wave) drift, no tides or inertial motion.

eddy_convergence.long_name: Warm-water & eddy convergence indicator (not a cyclone forecast)
eddy_convergence.on_demand: any IBR timestep (SST) with the fixed ARMOR3D vorticity
eddy_convergence.caveat: Warm-water & eddy convergence indicator, NOT a cyclone forecast or genesis probability. Tropical cyclogenesis is controlled by atmospheric conditions (low-level vorticity, humidity, vertical wind shear) that are not in these datasets. This layer only marks where warm surface water (SST >= 26.5 degC) coincides with cyclonic OCEAN geostrophic vorticity.
